newsitem.title: FRANCE: Banks help French bourse set record highs.
newsitem.headline: Banks help French bourse set record highs.

text.p: French shares hit an all-time high on Wednesday as renewed bank takeover speculation breathed extra life into a market which was already rising with other stock and bond markets.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed 2.82 percent, or 82.40 points, higher at 3,003.53 after hitting an all-time high of 3,026.99 intraday.
Financial shares, already helped by spillover optimism after news on Tuesday of a big German bank merger, were set alight after Deutsche Bank said it could make an acquisition in France.

They accounted for the lion's share of a hefty 11.6 billion francs in CAC-40 trading volume and gave extra verve to a market which was buoyed along with other European markets after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan said the economy was progressing with relatively modest inflation.

Shares in BNP bank, the most heavily traded, ended 10.14 percent up 274.9 francs and another of the biggest French banks, Societe Generale finished 6.1 percent higher at 783. Traders said both of these were improbable takeover targets.

CCF, which closed 7.84 percent higher at 282,0 francs, is seen as a possible target among larger banks but some analysts say takeover speculation based on general optimism rather than specifics and that acquisitions could focus on privatisation candidates Credit Lyonnais or CIC.
Carmaker Renault, another big volume gainer, added to Tuesday's advances to close up 8.62 percent at 179.0 francs after hitting year high of 187.8 intraday.

Brokers said the Renault stock, which rose on Tuesday, was helped by stream of positive analyst recommendations following the winding down of Vilvoorde Belgian plant closure saga and a view that the share appeared undervalued versus other rivals like Fiat and Volkswagen.
